what_it_does: ElasticMiter tackles a problem in hardware design automation: high-level synthesis (HLS) compilers take algorithmic descriptions and produce circuits automatically, but those circuits are hard to optimize because their scheduling is loose—tokens (units of computation) can arrive at different times without a global clock ordering. Standard equivalence checking assumes sequential circuits where every operation happens at a fixed cycle; elastic circuits don't have that structure. ElasticMiter defines a formal equivalence framework for elastic circuits: it builds a test harness (miter) that tries all possible token arrival timings and checks if two circuits produce identical results under every scenario. It then enables safe rewrites: each simplification rule is formally proven with the miter before applying it to the circuit, guaranteeing the simplified circuit is functionally identical.
